published_statement: Low gr-qc/9812067 (restating Wald Ch.10 / Hawking-Ellis Ch.7): Thm 2.4 -- for an initial data set (Sigma,h,K,J,rho) with matter described by u obeying a quasilinear symmetric hyperbolic system A^a nabla_a u + B u = c (eq. 2.2) and T depending only on u and g: (1) there is a unique smooth maximal development (M,g), globally hyperbolic with Cauchy surface i(Sigma); (2) if data agree on S subset Sigma and S' subset Sigma', D(i(S)) in M is isometric to D(i'(S')) in M'; (3) g depends continuously on the data. Cor 3.1/4.1: changing the data only inside K = J^+(p) cap Sigma leaves D(i(Sigma\K)) isometric; 'no gravitational influence propagates faster than light'. Sec.4: with ray cones inside the light cones, 'one cannot construct a warp drive which has the effect of making it possible to travel faster than light' -- one cannot reach an earlier point on a distant worldline than in the unaltered spacetime. Thm 4.2 adds the DEC: 'In the absence of exotic matter, it is impossible to construct a warp-drive.' Linear perturbations: bicharacteristics are the null geodesics of the background (p.4). Kontou-Sanders p.12: symmetric-hyperbolic Einstein-matter systems have 'a unique maximal globally hyperbolic solution (up to gauge equivalence) which depends continuously on the data'; the energy conditions used in the proof need not hold for T_ab; T_ab = 0 on O subset Sigma implies T_ab = 0 on D(O), even for a WEC-violating tachyonic scalar.
published_hypotheses: H1 classical GR, G_ab = 8 pi T_ab, with matter fields u obeying a FIXED quasilinear symmetric hyperbolic system A^a nabla_a u + B u = c (Low eq. 2.2; 'this theorem and corollary are true for a fixed equation of the form (2.2)')

H2 the matter ray cone (boundary of {v : v_a A^a positive definite}) lies inside (or on) the light cone of g -- 'the bicharacteristics of the matter equations are causal curves' (Low p.2); this, not an energy condition, is what bounds the domain of influence
H3 T_ab depends only on u and g (Low p.2)
H4 initial data satisfy the constraint equations (Low eq. 2.3) on a spacelike Cauchy surface Sigma; smooth data (Low: 'smooth'; low-regularity extensions not read here)

H5 the conclusion is about the maximal globally hyperbolic development: D(i(Sigma\K)) is isometric; the development need not be inextensible and nothing is asserted beyond its Cauchy horizon (Low p.2, remark after Thm 2.1)
H6 for the warp-drive statement: the 'decision' is modelled as a change of data only on K = J^+(p) cap Sigma for a single event p (Low p.5)
H7 for Low Thm 4.2 only: DEC on T_ab (Def 2.3) -- the tree does NOT use this step
hypothesis_drift: DROPPED H2 (matter characteristics causal): phase1.py:114-116 attributes 'characteristic speed c' to 'the metric' and says 'matter acting in a compact region cannot alter the metric outside its causal future' without any hypothesis on the matter sector. The source's bound comes from the matter ray cone lying inside g's light cone; rederive C6 shows a matter cone of speed v > c halves the floor to L/4c. The corridor is exotic by the tree's own record (phase1.py:30-35: formation.py's F1, negative enclosed mass), so the matter model is exactly the unspecified part. Evidence the other way (C7, Kontou-Sanders p.12): WEC/DEC violation does NOT by itself widen the domain of influence -- a tachyonic scalar has T_00 < 0 and characteristic speed c. So the tree's use survives exotic matter IF the exotic sector's principal part is causal; that is a named hypothesis the tree does not state.

DROPPED H1/H3 in part (classical, fixed hyperbolic matter equation, T a function of u and g only): phase1.py:111-128 and 309-317 state the result for any 'matter'. Quantum sources (semiclassical G = 8 pi <T>) are outside the theorem; the cached 2604.01047 establishes well-posedness only for a linearised forcing problem about Minkowski and says global well-posedness of the semiclassical system 'is not formally established'. Whether a curvature-coupled (nonminimal) source satisfies H3 is not established here (not read).

DROPPED H5 (maximal globally hyperbolic development): phase1.py:114-119 asserts the metric outside the causal future is unaltered, full stop. The source guarantees the isometry of D(Sigma\K) within the MGHD. For WEC-violating matter a compactly generated Cauchy horizon is not excluded by the Hawking/Topological-Censorship results (restated in Kay-Radzikowski-Wald gr-qc/9603012v2 p.3: 'the weak energy condition must be violated in any spacetime with a compactly generated Cauchy horizon with noncompact partial Cauchy surface S'), and beyond such a horizon no uniqueness is supplied. chronology.py is the tree's separate treatment; phase1 does not cite it as a hypothesis of Theorem 4.

ADDED/IMPLICIT single causal origin (H6 made silent): phase1.py:116-118 ('not complete before L/2c after the first action -- best case, acting from the midpoint') and phase1.py:310 ('L/2c: best case, acting from the midpoint'). This holds only if every metric-altering action is causally downstream of one event (Low's K = J^+(p) cap Sigma). Rederive C5: N independent actors already in place inside K, acting on prearranged clocks, complete at L/(2Nc) after the first action (N=10: 0.05 L/c). The floor then moves to placing the actors (>= L/2c from a single dispatch point), it does not vanish -- but the clause as written needs the hypothesis.

WEAKENED-TO-SCHEME (over-precision): phase1.py:326-340 and 474-476 compute single_transition_penalty() = 1.5 and print 'worse by exactly this factor'. The source bound (Low Sec.4) is: no earlier point of the destination worldline is reachable than in the unaltered spacetime, i.e. first arrival >= decision time + distance/c; the implied floor on the ratio is 1 (a tie, attainable by building on the light front and riding behind it, rederive C4b). 1.5 is the value of one scheme (midpoint, complete-then-traverse). The boolean single_transition_beats_light() = False AGREES with the source; the factor is a discrepancy of over-precision, not a refutation.

NO DRIFT (confirmation): 'characteristic speed c' is relative to the dynamical metric, and D(Sigma\K) is fixed by the UNALTERED data (Low Cor 4.1), so for a flat pre-existing background the floor L/2c in inertial coordinates is exact -- the change cannot move its own causal wall. The tree's 'coordinate length L' coincides with proper length only in the pre-existing flat metric, which is the one that sets the wall.

NO DRIFT: the tree does not use Low's DEC step (Thm 4.2 / H7), which later literature contests (Earman; Geroch 2010; Wong; Curiel 1405.0403; 2411.11050; Kontou-Sanders 2003.01815 p.8). phase1.py:124-126 explicitly calls Theorem 4 'the price of D2', not an energy-condition result.

rederivation.outcome: ALL CHECKS PASS (exit 0). C1: harmonic-gauge principal symbol g^{mn}k_m k_n = 0 gives phase speed c (null cone of g). C2: L/2c = 6.31150e7 s = 1.99999 Julian yr for L = 4 ly (tree pin 6.3113e7 is a last-digit discrepancy within tol). C3: single origin -- min over origin of completion = L/2c, attained only at the midpoint (sympy + 1e5 samples). C4: Low's bound gives first arrival >= t0 + d/c; tree scheme gives 1.5 L/c, a front-following scheme gives L/c -- 'never a lead' agrees, '1.5' is scheme-specific. C5: N independent pre-placed actors complete at L/(2Nc) after the first action -- the 'after the first action' clause needs a single causal origin. C6: a matter cone of speed v > c lowers the floor to L/(2 max(c,v)) -- the speed-c clause is a hypothesis on the matter. C7: tachyonic scalar T_00 = -1 < 0 with characteristic speed c -- energy-condition violation alone does not break causal propagation. C8: GW170817 bound moves nothing.

later_literature.what: Well-posed IVF for Einstein + symmetric-hyperbolic matter does not require any of the four energy conditions on T_ab; T_ab = 0 on O subset Sigma implies T_ab = 0 on D(O) even for the WEC-violating tachyonic scalar; DEC is not the right expression of 'no superluminal propagation' (Earman). Supports the tree applying causal propagation to exotic matter, provided H2 holds.

later_literature.ref: Curiel, arXiv:1405.0403 (2014), energy-conditions primer; and arXiv:2411.11050 lines 630-645
later_literature.what: The Hawking-Ellis conservation theorem only stops 'the edge of a vacuum' propagating superluminally (Wong); DEC is neither necessary nor sufficient for causal propagation (Earman, Geroch 2010). Contests Low's Thm 4.2 step 'superluminal ray cone only if DEC fails' -- a step the tree does not use.

later_literature.ref: Barzegar, Buchert & Vigneron, arXiv:2602.16495 (2026), Error 1 and Remark IV.38
later_literature.what: Warp spacetimes in ADM form with positive-definite spatial metric are NOT automatically globally hyperbolic (counterexamples: negative-mass Schwarzschild, AdS); global hyperbolicity must be proved (Choquet-Bruhat-Cotsakis 2002 criterion). Geroch's 'democracy of causal cones': matter cones wider than the light cone are not excluded by relativity's structure. Both bear on H2 and H5 as applied to exotic warp matter.

later_literature.ref: Galanda, Meda, Murro, Pinamonti & Schmid, arXiv:2604.01047 (2026)
later_literature.what: Semiclassical Einstein-Klein-Gordon: well-posedness shown only for a linearised forcing problem about Minkowski (higher-order nonlocal hyperbolic PDE), with late-time exponential instability; 'global well-posedness of the underlying equations is not formally established'. The classical domain-of-dependence theorem does not automatically cover quantum (e.g. Casimir) sources.

later_literature.what: Deforming a globally hyperbolic metric in a compact region to admit CTCs yields a compactly generated Cauchy horizon; such horizons (noncompact S) require WEC violation. Since the tree's corridor is WEC-violating, the MGHD hypothesis H5 is not automatic from energy conditions; the D(Sigma\K) isometry still holds inside the MGHD.

lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested. The result is a theorem of PDE and Lorentzian geometry; its conclusion depends on no measured number, only on the matter model's principal part (H2). What the authors (1952/1969; Low 1998) lacked: (a) a direct measurement of the speed of gravity -- supplied 2017 by GW170817, -3e-15 <= (v_gw-c)/c <= 7e-16; it confirms 'characteristic speed c' and moves the tree's floor by < 1e-14 relative (C8) -- evidence AGAINST M's hypothesis for this result; (b) any established model of the exotic (negative-energy) matter the corridor needs -- still lacking today: for classical exotic fields with causal principal part the theorem applies unchanged (C7, Kontou-Sanders), for quantum sources well-posedness is not established (2604.01047), and a matter sector with superluminal characteristics (Geroch's democracy of cones, 2602.16495 Remark IV.38) would lower the floor (C6). So missing data do not overturn the theorem; they leave OPEN whether its matter hypothesis H2 holds for whatever source would actually build the corridor. The later contesting (Earman/Geroch/Wong on the DEC) corrects Low's Thm 4.2 step, which the tree does not use.
grade_evidence: The theorem itself STANDS as restated (Low gr-qc/9812067 Thm 2.4/Cor 4.1, Kontou-Sanders 2003.01815 p.12); the re-derivation agrees (C1, C3, C4, C8) and no moved datum moves anything. The grade is NARROWED because the tree uses it on a larger class than the source proves: phase1.py:114-119/309-317 drops H2 (matter characteristics inside g's light cone) for a corridor that is exotic by the tree's own record (phase1.py:30-35), drops the classical/fixed-equation hypothesis (quantum sources outside), drops the MGHD scope (H5), and leaves implicit the single-causal-origin hypothesis without which 'not complete before L/2c after the first action' fails (C5: L/(2Nc)). Discrepancies recorded, not refutations: single_transition_penalty() = 1.5 is one scheme's value while the source's floor is ratio 1 (the False verdict agrees); pin 6.3113e7 vs computed 6.31150e7 s (inside tolerance). Not WRONG: no counterexample to the source theorem is shown, and every failure above is conditional on a hypothesis the source states and the tree omits. Source read via restatement only (alphaXiv quota; arxiv 403).
what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: phase1 Theorem 4 states H2 (the building matter's principal part has causal characteristics w.r.t. g), classical matter or an established well-posed semiclassical system, the MGHD scope, and a single causal origin for the L/2c clause (or recasts it as 'L/2c after the decision that dispatches the actors'), and replaces 'worse by exactly 1.5' with 'at least 1 (never a lead); 1.5 for the midpoint complete-then-traverse scheme'. To DATA-DEPENDENT/WRONG for the tree's use: an exhibited matter model that could build the corridor with superluminal characteristics (C6 then lowers the floor), or a well-posedness failure for the actual source. A reading of Choquet-Bruhat-Geroch 1969 / Hawking-Ellis Ch.7 at source that stated hypotheses beyond Low's restatement would revise the hypothesis list (currently READ-VIA-RESTATEMENT).
